Subject: MAP: tokenized unit-econ acceptance + simulation plan

Samantha —

Following our call, attaching a draft MAP worksheet (map-draft.xlsx) with the cost modeling section populated based on the traffic profile you shared in the demo. Key asks from our side to move the MAP to "cost-acceptance:"

- Confirm tokens-per-request distribution (median / 75th / 95th). We used a conservative 420 / 1,150 / 3,600 tokens for the patient-summary + follow-up prompts.
- Validate expected cache hit rate for templated prompts we discussed (we assumed 30% prefix/KV hit).
- Confirm target latency SLO for interactive flows (we modeled a 200ms tail target with batching turned on).

What Redwood will do once we have your confirmation:
- Run a fast simulation on a 7-day sample of traffic you provide (we can take CSV) to produce an expected tokens-per-dollar curve for three model variants (base fp16, 4-bit quant, and a streaming-optimized variant).
- Surface a canary plan: start with 10k requests/day, measure observed cache hit / batching distribution, and reconcile actual $/M tokens against the model.
- Produce an acceptance gate: 20% deviation from modeled unit cost at 95th percentile tokens per request triggers an ops pause and remediation.

Proposed high-level timeline (editable in the MAP):
- Day 0 (today): share MAP-draft and sample CSV schema (attached).
- Day 2: Clause Health returns a 7-day sample CSV + any clarifying notes.
- Day 4–6: Redwood runs simulation and posts results + recommendations.
- Day 7–10: Canary rollout and final acceptance decision.

If this timeline works for you, confirm and we'll stamp the MAP with the acceptance criteria and add the simulation spec.

Thanks,

Thanks Grace — this looks reasonable. A couple quick clarifications before we pull the 7-day sample: 

1) Tokens per request: the 95th percentile you used seems high; our UI stitching sometimes creates longer contexts (doctor notes + history). We can run a quick histogram export. Expectation: 95th ~ 2,800 in our last export, not 3,600. I'll confirm.

2) Cache hit definition: when you say 30% prefix/KV hit, do you mean identical prompt prefix (templated intake) or semantic caching? Most tappable savings for us will come from templated prompts for discharge summaries (identical prefix) — those should be high (~45–50% on our projected rollout).

3) Simulation: we can deliver a CSV but need to confirm PII sanitization scope. Will Redwood accept a hashed patient id + redacted clinical text? We can't send PHI raw.

We can aim to send the sanitized 7-day sample by Thursday EOD (Aug 27). If you can run the simulation same day and share preliminary numbers, that would be great.

Samantha Lee

Samantha — great questions. Quick answers and the plan we propose to keep the MAP moving: 

1) Tokens percentiles: please send the histogram export. In parallel we'll run a small transformer-based token estimator on redacted samples if you prefer (we don't need PHI to estimate token lengths).

2) Cache hit semantics: we were referencing identical-prefix (template) caching — good to hear Clause projects 45–50% for discharge templates. For the simulation we'll parameterize cache hit rate as an input (0–60%), so yourown PLG can see sensitivity.

3) Sanitization: hashed patient IDs + redacted clinical text is fine. We only need enough signal to reconstruct request lengths, prompt templates, and time-of-day distribution.

Attached is sample_traffic_profile.csv — it's the schema we expect (timestamp, hashed_user_id, prompt_template_id, tokens_total, model_hint). If you attach your sanitized export to this thread, Karthik will run the sim and post a Results Spec.

Preliminary cost assumptions we used in the MAP-draft (for transparency):
- Base model (fp16): $18 per 1M input+output tokens
- Quantized 4-bit variant: $9 per 1M tokens (est. 1.9x throughput improvement)
- Streaming optimized variant: $14 per 1M tokens but improves tail latency for long requests

Acceptance gate (draft): simulated 95th-percentile unit cost must be within +/−20% of the modeled value for us to sign off. If mismatch >20%, we'll propose tuning (higher cache, different batching) and a re-run window of 3 business days.

Proposed schedule if you can deliver sample Thu EOD (Aug 27):
- Thu (Aug 27): Karthik ingests sample, runs sim, posts results spec by 6pm PT.
- Fri (Aug 28): Joint readout + adjust MAP assumptions.
- Mon (Aug 31)–Wed (Sep 2): Canary kickoff and 72-hour observation window.

Adding a few technical checks and what I'll run during the sim: 

- Tokenization sanity: I'll run both the exact tokenizer and a lightweight estimator so we can quantify estimator error; this will reconcile your 2,800 vs our 3,600 outlier.
- Cache model: we'll parameterize two caches: (a) prefix/template cache (zero-shot exact match) and (b) KV reuse for repeated context windows. The simulation will output separate savings lines for each so decision-makers can see where savings come from.
- Batching assumptions: default schedule will be continuous batching with max_batch_size=128 and target_batch_latency=30ms. We'll also run a latency-constrained simulation with max_batch_size=32 to show cost/latency trade-offs.
- Quantization effects: sim will apply a model-specific tokens-per-second multiplier and per-token cost delta for the 4-bit path. We'll produce cost curves for three model variants.

Deliverables by EOD Thu (per Ben's timeline):
1) sim-results-spec.md (what I run + assumptions)
2) tokens-per-dollar curve CSV (by model variant and cache hit % grid)
3) short readout deck (3 slides) with recommended canary thresholds and acceptance gates

A couple of operational notes for the MAP:
- If observed cache hit during canary is >10% different from the sim input, we automate an ops pause and a 24-hour triage window.
- If batching behavior in production yields <60% of simulated batching efficiency (due to request spread), we'll recommend a routing tweak or small client-side buffering change.

I'll start once we have the sanitized CSV. Grace/Ben — flag if you want me to include memory/KV cache size constraints in the spec.
